title: OTT expands creative horizons, breaks language barriers and connects audiences: IFFI OTT Awards Jury
subtitle: Jury members discuss evolving narratives, character-driven storytelling and opportunities for emerging talent in the digital space
body_text:
Posted On: 28 NOV 2026 2:07PM by PIB Mumbai Release ID: 2342996 Views: 67 A A Print Share X Facebook Instagram WhatsApp Copy Article Link
Read in: English
Goa, 28 November 2026 The Jury for the Best Web Series (OTT) Award at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, comprising Chairman JD Majethia and members Krishna Hebbale, Shailendra Jha and Garima Wahal shared their perspectives on the evolution of OTT storytelling, changing audience preferences and the opportunities digital platforms have opened up for creative talent. Speaking about the growth of the entertainment industry, Jury Chairman JD Majethia said that the expansion of internet access and OTT platforms had enabled audiences to explore content from different countries and regions of India, creating new possibilities for storytelling. He described Goa and IFFI as a platform capable of taking India's entertainment industry forward. Reflecting on the jury's experience of evaluating web series for the OTT Award, Majethia said that each member brought a distinct perspective to the process. The evaluation considered storytelling, characterisation, performances, execution and the lasting impression a series created. He noted the growing prominence of ensemble casts and character-driven narratives, adding that the extended format of web series offered greater freedom to develop stories and characters. He also observed that the COVID-19 pandemic had given a significant boost to the sector. Jury member Krishna Hebbale highlighted the rising standards of writing in web series, noting that audiences could quickly move to another show if a story failed to hold their attention. Comparing acting in a web series to playing a Test match, he said the format demanded sustained skill while offering actors greater scope to explore their characters. Shailendra Jha said OTT platforms had opened doors for creative voices that may not have found opportunities in the conventional entertainment industry. He highlighted the format's emphasis on multiple, evolving characters, with viewers becoming invested in their journeys and eager to follow what happens next. He also noted that subtitles were helping break language barriers and enabling audiences to discover stories from different linguistic backgrounds. Jury member Garima Wahal observed that web series offered audiences a window into India's diversity through a wide range of stories, emotions and creative talent. Comparing the experience to reading a book, she said the format enabled a more intimate connection with viewers. She added that the growing popularity of different genres and the flexibility to watch entire stories through binge-watching had expanded the scope of entertainment and created opportunities for emerging talent. The jury members underscored the role of OTT platforms in encouraging experimentation, broadening creative opportunities and bringing diverse stories and voices to audiences across the country. The discussion at the 57th IFFI reflected the festival's larger vision of celebrating diverse forms of storytelling and recognising the changing landscape of cinema and entertainment. By bringing together voices from across the industry, IFFI continues to provide a platform for conversations on emerging formats, evolving creative practices and the opportunities shaping the future of India's audiovisual sector. The press conference was moderated by Shri Mahesh Kumar.
